Beige Book (April 2022) context for the May 4, 2022 FOMC statement:
- Overall activity: District reports point to modest-to-moderate expansion, with consumer spending and services improving and manufacturing contributing to growth. Several Districts (e.g., New York) cited growth even as supply disruptions persisted.
- Labor markets and wages: Employment continued to rise amid very tight labor markets and persistent worker shortages; wage growth was strong and broad-based—consistent with the FOMC’s “robust job gains” and ongoing inflation pressures.
- Prices: Input and output prices were elevated and widespread, with higher energy costs and freight/fuel surcharges feeding through as firms passed on costs.
- Sectoral detail: Housing demand showed signs of cooling as mortgage rates rose; auto sales remained constrained by low inventories. CRE credit remained available—multifamily solid, retail/industrial steady—while office occupancy remained a challenge.
- Credit channel (SLOOS overlay): Banks eased C&I standards for large/mid-market firms and saw stronger loan demand; consumer credit standards eased with firmer auto/HELOC demand, partially offset by some tightening at foreign banks. Net effect: bank intermediation still supportive of near-term activity.
- Outlook and risks: Businesses flagged downside risks from Ukraine, inflation, and supply chain issues, but near-term demand remained resilient.

Implication for tone relative to the statement: The Beige Book’s modest expansion and supportive bank credit temper the downside emphasis of the FOMC statement, but broad price pressures and uncertainty keep the bias negative. Slightly less negative than an FSR-only or statement-only read.
